title: Getting Started with multiGGM
text: multiGGM package implements Bayesian method Peterson, Stingo & Vannucci (2015, JASA) joint inference multiple Gaussian graphical models (GGMs). Given data KK groups, method simultaneously estimates group-specific precision matrices Ωk\Omega_k associated conditional independence graphs GkG_k, borrowing strength across groups Markov random field (MRF) prior. vignette walks : Simulating multi-group data known graph structure Fitting model multiggm_mcmc() Checking convergence Extracting interpreting results Comparing estimated graphs ground truth Running summarizing multiple MCMC chains

title: Getting Started with multiGGM
text: generate data two groups p=15p = 15 variables n=100n = 100 observations , using banded (AR-2) graph structure.
code: library(multiGGM)  sim <- simulate_multiggm(   K = 2, p = 20, n = 100,   graph_type = "random",   perturb_prob = 0.1,   seed = 42 )  cat("True edge counts:\n") #> True edge counts: for (k in 1:sim$K) {   adj_k <- sim$adj_list[[k]]   cat(sprintf("  Group %d: %d edges\n", k, sum(adj_k[upper.tri(adj_k)]))) } #>   Group 1: 15 edges #>   Group 2: 32 edges

text: Overlaying trace plots multiple chains one effective visual convergence diagnostics. Chains converged mix overlap, chains stuck different modes show persistent separation.
code: library(ggplot2)  # Build a combined edge-count trace from all chains trace_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(fit_mc$nchains), function(ch) {   ec <- edge_counts(fit_mc, chain = ch)   data.frame(     iteration = seq_len(nrow(ec)),     edges     = ec[, 1],     chain     = paste("Chain", ch),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }))  ggplot(trace_df, aes(x = iteration, y = edges, color = chain)) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +   labs(title = "Edge count trace (Group 1) across chains",        x = "Iteration (post-burnin)", y = "Number of edges") +   theme_minimal() # Overlay theta traces from all chains theta_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(fit_mc$nchains), function(ch) {   data.frame(     iteration = seq_len(dim(fit_mc$chains[[ch]]$Theta_save)[3]),     theta     = fit_mc$chains[[ch]]$Theta_save[1, 2, ],     chain     = paste("Chain", ch),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }))  ggplot(theta_df, aes(x = iteration, y = theta, color = chain)) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +   labs(title = "Trace: theta[1,2] across chains",        x = "Iteration (post-burnin)", y = "theta[1,2]") +   theme_minimal()

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
text: Version 0.2.0 multiGGM adds second inference method: spike--slab continuous shrinkage prior Shaddox et al. (2018, Statistics Biosciences). method replaces G-Wishart prior Wang-Li exchange algorithm column-wise Gibbs sampler scales graphs p>100p > 100 nodes. Select method via method argument: methods estimate quantities—group-specific precision matrices Ωk\Omega_k, adjacency matrices GkG_k, graph similarity parameters θkm\theta_{km}, edge-specific log-odds νij\nu_{ij}—output objects identical structure. post-processing functions (pip_edges, posterior_pcor, plot, etc.) work either method.
code: # Original G-Wishart method (default, best for small p) fit_gw <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list, method = "gwishart")  # Scalable SSVS method (for larger p) fit_ssvs <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list, method = "ssvs")

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
text: methods share Markov random field (MRF) prior borrows strength across groups, Metropolis-Hastings updates graph similarity parameters θkm\theta_{km} edge-specific log-odds νij\nu_{ij}. differ precision matrices Ωk\Omega_k graphs GkG_k sampled.

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
text: original Peterson et al. (2015) approach places G-Wishart prior Ωk∣Gk∼WG(b,D)\Omega_k \mid G_k \sim W_G(b, D) precision matrix. Sampling proceeds via Wang-Li (2012) exchange algorithm: Compute Bernoulli proposal probability G-Wishart posterior ratio (log_H) MRF similarity term. proposed graph differs, sample new precision matrix G-Wishart conditional (GWishart_NOij_Gibbs). Accept reject via exchange ratio involving G-Wishart pdf evaluations (log_GWishart_NOij_pdf). Update precision matrix posterior conditional. edges: refresh full precision matrix via BIPS (Block Incomplete Partial correlation Sampling) using maximal clique decomposition (GWishart_BIPS_maximumClique). requires O(p2)O(p^2) edge proposals per group, involving O(p2)O(p^2)–O(p3)O(p^3) matrix operations, plus additional O(p2)O(p^2) BIPS step.

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
text: Shaddox et al. (2018) approach replaces G-Wishart prior spike--slab normal prior -diagonal precision element: ωk,ij∣zk,ij∼(1−zk,ij)⋅N(0,v0)+zk,ij⋅N(0,v1)\omega_{k,ij} \mid z_{k,ij} \sim (1 - z_{k,ij}) \cdot N(0, v_0) + z_{k,ij} \cdot N(0, v_1) v0≪v1v_0 \ll v_1 (spike vs. slab), exponential prior diagonal elements: ωk,ii∼Exp(λ/2)\omega_{k,ii} \sim \text{Exp}(\lambda/2). prior tractable normalizing constant, sampling uses direct column-wise Gibbs sweep: Compute Schur complement C11−1=Σ11−Σ12Σ12⊤/ΣiiC_{11}^{-1} = \Sigma_{11} - \Sigma_{12}\Sigma_{12}^\top / \Sigma_{ii} current covariance (matrix inversion needed). Form posterior precision Ci=(Sii+λ)⋅C11−1+diag(1/τ)C_i = (S_{ii} + \lambda) \cdot C_{11}^{-1} + \text{diag}(1/\tau), τ\tau contains v0v_0 v1v_1 depending current edge inclusion. Sample -diagonal column multivariate normal conditional: ϵ∼N(μi,Ci−1)\epsilon \sim N(\mu_i, C_i^{-1}). Sample diagonal Gamma conditional: γ∼Gamma(nk/2+1,(Sii+λ)/2)\gamma \sim \text{Gamma}(n_k/2 + 1,\; (S_{ii} + \lambda)/2). Rank-1 covariance update: update Σ\Sigma directly new column without full matrix inversion. Update edge indicators zz via posterior spike-slab odds, incorporating MRF prior analytically conditional inclusion probability. exchange algorithm, BIPS clique step, trans-dimensional moves. iteration costs O(p)O(p) column sweeps, O(p2)O(p^2) Cholesky solve rank-1 update, giving O(p3)O(p^3) total per group per iteration.

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
text: MRF normalizing constant C(θ,νij)C(\theta, \nu_{ij}) uses exact enumeration {0,1}K\{0,1\}^K binary vectors (feasible KK small). θkm\theta_{km} update (-model spike/slab toggle + within-model Gamma proposal) νij\nu_{ij} update (MH Beta proposal) identical methods.

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
text: SSVS-specific hyperparameters defaults : variance inflation ratio h=v1/v0=2500h = v_1 / v_0 = 2500 controls edge selection sensitivity. prior edge inclusion probability adapts dimension: π=2/(p−1)\pi = 2/(p-1), favors sparse graphs pp grows. defaults follow Wang (2015, Bayesian Analysis), “Scaling : stochastic search structure learning graphical models,” introduced SSVS approach single GGMs. multiGGM implementation extends multiple graphs adding MRF-coupled edge indicators.

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
text: v0 v1: defaults work well standardized data. data different scale, may need adjust. larger v1 allows stronger partial correlations; smaller v0 provides stricter edge selection. lambda: Controls diagonal shrinkage. default 1 generally safe. Increasing lambda adds regularization diagonal. burnin nsave: SSVS sampler typically mixes faster G-Wishart, may need fewer iterations. Start burnin = 5000, nsave = 5000 check trace plots. production runs, Shaddox et al. (2018) used burnin = 40000, nsave = 80000. b: Decrease b denser graphs (e.g., Beta(1, 1) uniform prior edge probability) increase sparser graphs (e.g., Beta(1, 9) $$10% prior edge probability).

title: Scalable Inference with the SSVS Method
code: fit <- multiggm_mcmc(   data_list = sim$data_list,   method    = "ssvs",   hyper     = list(     v0    = 0.01^2,    # tighter spike     v1    = 100^2 * 0.01^2,  # wider slab     lambda = 2,        # stronger diagonal shrinkage     a = 1, b = 9,      # sparser prior (Beta(1,9))     alpha = 2, beta = 5,     w = 0.5,           # less certain groups are related     alpha_prop = 1, beta_prop = 1   ),   burnin = 5000,   nsave  = 5000,   seed   = 42 )

title: Log normalizing constant for the MRF prior (per edge) — calc_mrf_logC
text:
Computes log normalizing constant \(\log C(\Theta, 
u)\) Markov random field prior graph edge indicators, defined Peterson et al. (2015), Equation 3.2: $$C(\Theta, 
u) = \sum_{g \{0,1\}^K} \exp(
u \cdot \mathbf{1}'g + g'\Theta g)$$ computational hot spot MRF prior evaluation implemented C++ via RcppArmadillo performance.

title: Log normalizing constant for the MRF prior (per edge) — calc_mrf_logC

title: Log normalizing constant for the MRF prior (per edge) — calc_mrf_logC

text: single chain (nchains = 1), object class "multiggm_fit" following components: K Integer; number groups. p Integer; number variables (nodes). C_save Numeric array [p, p, K, nsave]; posterior draws precision matrices \(\Omega_k\). C_save[,,k,s] precision matrix group k saved iteration s. Theta_save Numeric array [K, K, nsave]; posterior draws graph similarity parameters \(\theta_{km}\). Theta_save[k,m,s] measures similarity graphs k m iteration s. Values > 0 indicate model borrows strength groups. nu_save Numeric array [p, p, nsave]; posterior draws edge-specific log-odds parameters \(\nu_{ij}\). nu_save[,j,s] controls baseline edge inclusion probability edge (,j) across groups iteration s. ar_gamma Numeric matrix [K, K]; acceptance rates -model (spike-slab toggle) moves \(\theta_{km}\). Upper triangle . ar_theta Numeric matrix [K, K]; acceptance rates within-model (slab--slab) moves \(\theta_{km}\). Upper triangle . meaningful \(\theta_{km} > 0\). ar_nu Numeric matrix [p, p]; acceptance rates \(\nu_{ij}\) MH updates. Upper triangle . hyper Named list hyperparameters used. call matched function call. multiple chains (nchains > 1), object class "multiggm_fit_list" components: chains List nchains multiggm_fit objects. call matched function call. K Integer; number groups. nchains Integer; number chains.

title: Fit multiple Gaussian graphical models via MCMC — multiggm_mcmc
text: Method selection: method = "gwishart" uses G-Wishart prior precision matrices Wang-Li (2012) exchange algorithm. Accurate computationally expensive \(p > 30\). method = "ssvs" replaces spike--slab normal prior, enabling column-wise Gibbs sampling scales \(p > 100\). methods use MRF prior borrowing strength across groups. hyper list may contain following: Common hyperparameters (methods): , b Beta(, b) prior \(q_{ij} = \text{logit}^{-1}(\nu_{ij})\). Default = 1, b = 4, giving prior edge probability \(\approx 0.20\). alpha, beta Gamma(shape = alpha, rate = beta) slab prior \(\theta_{km}\). NOTE: beta RATE parameter. Default alpha = 2, beta = 5, giving mean = 0.4. w Bernoulli prior probability \(\gamma_{km} = 1\) (graph similarity active). Default 0.9 (strong prior belief groups related). alpha_prop, beta_prop Gamma(shape = alpha_prop, rate = beta_prop) proposal \(\theta_{km}\). Default alpha_prop = 2, beta_prop = 5 G-Wishart; alpha_prop = 1, beta_prop = 1 SSVS. G-Wishart-specific hyperparameters (method = "gwishart"): b_prior G-Wishart degrees freedom (default 3). D_prior G-Wishart scale matrix, p x p (default diag(p)). SSVS-specific hyperparameters (method = "ssvs" "ssvs_platform"): v0 Spike variance -diagonal precision elements (default 0.02^2 = 0.0004). v1 Slab variance -diagonal precision elements (default 50^2 * v0 = 1.0). lambda Exponential rate hyperparameter diagonal elements (default 1). Platform-level hyperparameters (method = "ssvs_platform" ): eta, kappa Gamma(shape = eta, scale = kappa) slab prior platform similarity \(\Phi_{st}\). Default eta = 4, kappa = 5. eta_prop, kappa_prop Gamma proposal \(\Phi_{st}\). Default eta_prop = 1, kappa_prop = 1. d, f Beta(d, f) prior platform-level edge log-odds \(w_{km}\). Default d = 1, f = 19. d_prop, f_prop Beta proposal \(w_{km}\). Default d_prop = 2, f_prop = 4. u_prior Bernoulli prior probability \(P(\zeta_{st} = 1)\). Default 0.1.
